verdict: Paychex grew revenue 6% to $1.6 billion and expanded its operating margin to 38%, as double-digit growth in its PEO and insurance business outpaced the core payroll business.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Total revenue $1.63B, up from $1.54B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Up 14% YoY; adjusted EPS was $1.34, excluding acquisition costs

kpis.label: PEO & Insurance revenue
kpis.note: Up 12% YoY — the growth engine this quarter

kpis.label: Operating margin
kpis.note: Up from 35.2% a year ago (42.0% adjusted)

segments.name: Management Solutions
segments.note: Payroll processing and HR software for small and mid-sized businesses — the core business, up 4% on higher revenue per client.

segments.name: PEO & Insurance Solutions
segments.note: Paychex becomes the employer of record for client staff (a professional employer organization) and sells workplace insurance — up 12% on more worksite employees.

segments.name: Interest on funds held for clients
segments.note: Interest earned on payroll money Paychex briefly holds before paying employees and tax agencies — up 5%.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, service staff overhead and running the company — actually down 1% YoY despite revenue growth.

otherDetail: A net $54M drag: $65M of interest expense on Paychex's borrowings, partly offset by $11M of other income.
footerNote: Paychex reports only two expense lines — cost of service revenue and selling, general & administrative — so the flow mirrors that structure instead of inventing an R&D split.
oneTimers: Acquisition-related costs of $65.5M (mainly from the Paycor deal) are inside GAAP results; excluding them, adjusted operating income was $684.7M and adjusted EPS $1.34.

takeaways.title: PEO is the growth engine
takeaways.text: PEO and Insurance revenue grew 12% to $368M on more worksite employees and higher insurance volumes — three times the growth rate of the core payroll business.

takeaways.title: Margins expanded
takeaways.text: Operating margin rose to 38.0% from 35.2% as revenue grew and acquisition-related costs fell versus a year ago. Adjusted margin was 42.0%.

takeaways.title: EPS grew twice as fast as revenue
takeaways.text: Diluted EPS rose 14% to $1.21 — margin gains and fewer shares outstanding turned 6% revenue growth into double-digit profit growth.
